subject: On-prem K8s readiness: ephemeral NVMe scratch and nodeclass provisioning
messages:
From: Daniel Rhee <ops@edgehost.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: K8s provisioning questions ahead of on-site

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the prep call. We're finalizing hardware and need quick confirmation on how Redwood expects to use ephemeral PVs for KV cache overrides and model shard temp files. Our ops team prefers local NVMe for scratch. What's the recommended node class labeling and eviction behavior?

Current plan: 8 x A100 nodes, local 1.6TB NVMe per node, air-gapped cluster. We'll share rack topology tomorrow.

Regards,
Daniel
Operations Lead, EdgeHost Systems

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Rhee <ops@edgehost.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: K8s provisioning questions ahead of on-site

Daniel —

Appreciate the hardware summary. Short answers here; attached YAML + sketch has the details we should validate on-site. High-level recommendations:

- Scratch storage: use node-local NVMe for ephemeral model shards and KV cache; expose via a local CSI driver (volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer) so scheduler places pods on nodes with NVMe
- Node labels: node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass=scratch-ssd and node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass=steady-ssd for long-running serving nodes
- Taints: mark scratch nodes with scratch=true:NoSchedule and allow tolerant pods for model loaders and batch jobs
- Eviction: configure kubelet.evictionHard nodefs.available=5%, imagefs.available=10% and set podPriority for inference pods to protect them from eviction where possible
- Reclaim policy: use Retain on debug volumes and Delete for strictly ephemeral shards; rely on job/DaemonSet cleanup hooks to clear /scratch on termination

On-site checklist: NVMe namespace mapping, NVMe driver and firmware versions, kernel I/O scheduler settings (noop/none for low latency), and BIOS power policies. We'll also bring a small DaemonSet that publishes NVMe topology to a central ConfigMap for scheduler constraints.

I'll loop Dev for CSI / device-plugin details and Sean for the capacity planning metrics.

-Kim

Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Rhee <ops@edgehost.com>

Subject: Re: K8s provisioning questions ahead of on-site

Thanks Kim — that helps a lot. Couple quick follow-ups from our infra team:

- For model shards ~200GB each, do you recommend binding a hostPath per pod, direct-attached NVMe, or the local CSI approach you mentioned? We want predictable affinity but minimum manual ops.
- For bursty load patterns (nightly batch loads + daytime steady inference), how do you suggest shaping node taints/tolerations and autoscaler policies so we don't evict steady-serving pods during batch spikes?

We'll produce firmware/driver inventory before the visit. Also attaching a short rack map for reference.

—Daniel

From: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Daniel Rhee <ops@edgehost.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: K8s provisioning questions ahead of on-site

Daniel — quick technical clarifications inline:

- For ~200GB shards we prefer the local CSI pattern that binds volumes to the node (CSI with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer and immediate provisioning). This gives scheduler visibility and allows PVs to remain tied to node for debugging; it's safer than hostPath and more manageable than ad-hoc direct-attach if you want Kubernetes-level lifecycle control.
- Taint/Nodeclass strategy: two nodeclasses — scratch-ssd (taint: scratch=yes:NoSchedule, purpose: model-loading & temporary shard staging) and steady-ssd (no taint, purpose: steady inference). Use Cluster Autoscaler with node group labels so scale-up respects nodeclass intent.
- Eviction and probes: add preStop hook to flush KV cache to local durable store when possible and use liveness/readinessProbes tuned for model load durations.
- Distribution: use PodTopologySpreadConstraints to avoid concentrating model copies on a single rack; include zone and host topology keys if available.

I'll attach a sample DaemonSet for NVMe discovery and a minimal provisioning-variables.yaml (see attachments). On-site we'll validate NVMe multipath and confirm kernel 5.x+ settings.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
